findings.title: MAL-2026-10727: Malicious code in axios-test-one (npm)
findings.summary_md: OSV recorded MAL-2026-10727 on July 16, 2026 from an Amazon Inspector report about axios-test-one, an npm package that copied the real axios description, repository URL, homepage, README and CHANGELOG. The advisory says the package declared a runtime dependency on the author-controlled telemetry-metrics package and invoked its plugin on every axios GET request through lib/helpers/telemetry.js and the bundled dist/node/axios.cjs. It notes that consumers load telemetry-metrics before calling any API, so ordinary GET traffic reaches that third-party code path.

findings.title: 13 Malicious NuGet Packages Target .NET Developers With Fake Job Assessments
findings.summary_md: Socket published the primary research on November 23, 2026, naming 13 malicious NuGet packages, 28 versions and four publisher accounts behind fake Windows .NET job assessments. It describes a build analyzer that runs a bundled DLL after every build, stages OskSupport.dll into %LOCALAPPDATA%\osk\ next to a copied osk.exe, and a WinUI FileButton that later starts that copy with a hidden window. It also details WinUI.Button 1.0.0, still listed at publication with about 160 downloads, whose control fetches avast.exe through the GitHub contents API and saves it as %TEMP%\Launcher.exe. Socket did not attribute the campaign and found no indicator overlap with published Contagious Interview reporting.

findings.title: Fake .NET job tests ship malicious NuGet button controls
findings.summary_md: Corgea published a technical teardown on November 24, 2026 that catalogs the affected NuGet versions and their npm predecessors. It confirms the repository-local restore source RestoreAdditionalProjectSources, the ForceExecuteNonExistenFile output that keeps the targets file running on every build, and the paths %LOCALAPPDATA%\osk\OskSupport.dll and %TEMP%\Launcher.exe. It reports that WinUI.Button 1.0.0 was still installable on November 23 and gone from NuGet when checked on November 24, while the other 12 packages had already been removed.

findings.title: Fake Job Assessments Linked to 13 Malicious NuGet Packages
findings.summary_md: Brandefense published a summary on November 24, 2026 noting that Socket had reported 13 linked packages and that NuGet had removed 12 while WinUI.Button 1.0.0 remained listed at publication. It frames the risk as code executing during a build or when an application creates a UI control, and maps the behavior to MSBuild execution, malicious library execution and DLL side-loading techniques. It cautions that restoring a package alone is not proof of compromise, that the side-load was not tested end to end, and that no victim count was provided.

findings.title: NuGet fake job assessment build hijack threat: detection, logs and IOCs
findings.summary_md: Spectrum Delta Research published a detection-focused threat entry on November 24, 2026 covering the same unattributed operation. It ties each stage to telemetry: restore logs showing repository-local package sources and committed .nupkg files, process events for dotnet.exe launched on MSBuildAnalyzer.dll under a NuGet lib folder, and file events for %LOCALAPPDATA%\osk\OskSupport.dll. It lists hunts for GitHub contents API traffic with log1.dat or log2.dat, commit messages downloading new version and Backup, user agents MyUpdater and CppHttp/1.0, and PowerShell Win32_ShadowCopy creation.
